subject.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup

question: Should OpenClaw accept a guarded backup-startup cleanup policy for one-hour-old OpenClaw-owned temp artifacts once this PR covers prior timestamped default outputs?
rationale: The code defect is concrete, but automatic deletion of stale backup temp artifacts changes operator cleanup and recovery expectations, especially for ownerless artifacts left by older versions.

options.title: Repair and accept guarded sweep
options.body: Broaden the matcher, preserve UUID/age/owner/output-directory scoping, rebase onto current main, and then accept the startup cleanup as the backup self-healing policy.

options.title: Accept fixed-output cleanup only
options.body: Land only the stable-basename behavior and explicitly leave default timestamped archive temps to a follow-up, accepting that the main user path remains partially unresolved.

options.title: Pause cleanup policy
options.body: Pause or close until maintainers choose a different recovery/debugging policy for stale backup temp artifacts.

recommendation.title: Repair and accept guarded sweep
recommendation.body: Broaden the matcher, preserve UUID/age/owner/output-directory scoping, rebase onto current main, and then accept the startup cleanup as the backup self-healing policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup retry cleanup work makes this the most current routing signal for the rebase and destructive-cleanup policy question.
